To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HLA-G is a unique MHC molecule that displays a low degree of polymorphism in its coding region but a high degree of polymorphism at the 5′ untranslated region and 3′untranslated region that may influence the expression of HLA-G and its function in different pathological conditions.

1) The HLA-G polymorphic sites may have a role in the regulation of HLA-G expression; 2) The HLA region has been under balancing selection; 3) The HLA class Ib genes are under positive selection; 4) The HLA polymorphism may influence the HLA-G function; 5) The HLA genes may influence disease susceptibility.
the HLA-G gene polymorphism is restricted to the regulatory regions and that the HLA region has been shaped by the interplay between positive selection and balancing selection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, analysis and functional characterization of HLA-G polymorphisms, and their association with diseases.
the study of the polymorphism in the HLA-G gene and its implications in the modulation of gene function, regulation, and evolution.
the role of HLA-G in reproduction, pregnancy, transplantation, and tumor biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HLA-G gene is a polymorphic gene with a complex structure and function that may be influenced by polymorphic sites in the promoter and 5′ untranslated region.
the HLA-G gene is polymorphic and that the polymorphism may influence its biological properties and its association to disease.
the low polymorphism of HILA-G is due to a strong selective pressure, whereas the high polymorphism of the regulatory region is due to balancing selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the polymorphism of the regulatory regions of the gene is associated with the modulation of gene expression, and this may be the main factor responsible for the different biological properties and the disease association observed for the HLA-G allele.
HLA-G is an immunoregulatory molecule with a unique role in the immune response, whose function is influenced by polymorphic sites, particularly in the promoter and in the 3′ untranslated region.
the polymorphic sites of HLA-G have been studied in experimental models as well as in pathological conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HLA-G polymorphism may influence the regulation and function of this molecule and that the study of the polymorphic sites of the HLA region is of great interest for a better understanding of its function, regulation and evolution.
the HLA-G gene has been subjected to strong selection pressure, both in coding and in regulatory regions.
the HLA-G locus has been subjected to strong evolutionary constraints, which may be related with its immunomodulatory function.
